report.source_text: Histologic examination of the biopsy from his descending colon (Fig. 1) showed cryptitis and crypt abscesses. A biopsy from his rectum (Fig. 2) showed early crypt distortion and basal plasmacytosis. In the absence of an infectious etiology, these findings were suggestive of a chronic colitis and/or IBD. There were no granulomas, vasculitis, or dysplasia.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 54-year-old African-American man presented initially with extraintestinal inflammatory manifestations including right eye anterior uveitis, right ear auricular chondritis, and wrist pain and redness. Subsequently, he developed gastrointestinal symptoms typical of inflammatory bowel disease, including hematochezia, left lower quadrant pain, and a perirectal abscess with fistula. Serologic testing showed positive c-ANCA at a titer of 1:40 with elevated proteinase 3 by ELISA, with negative ANA, AMA, ASMA, RF, anti-CCP, and normal complements. Colonoscopy with biopsy demonstrated cryptitis, crypt abscesses, early crypt distortion, and basal plasmacytosis consistent with chronic colitis and IBD, without granulomas or vasculitis. Despite lack of documented joint imaging results, the clinical presentation coupled with serology and histopathology supports the diagnosis of c-ANCA positive IBD preceded by prominent extraintestinal inflammatory manifestations.
